patterns.name: Context-Preserving Push
patterns.feelsLike: The current view slides aside while the new view slides in from the right, maintaining spatial context.
useWhen: Navigating deeper into a hierarchy (e.g., list → detail)
User expects to return to the previous context

prompts.swiftui:
Create a navigation push transition in SwiftUI with:
- Spring animation (damping: 0.85, response: 0.35)
- The outgoing view translates left by 30% with slight opacity fade to 0.8
- The incoming view slides from the right edge (100% → 0%)
- Support interactive swipe-back gesture using simultaneousGesture
- Use matchedGeometryEffect for any shared elements like navigation bar titles
- Make the transition interruptible mid-animation
- Add subtle shadow on the incoming view for depth
prompts.web:
Create a navigation push transition in HTML/CSS/JS with:
- CSS transition using cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) for spring-like feel
- Duration: 350ms
- Outgoing view: translateX(-30%) with opacity 0.8
- Incoming view: translateX(100%) → translateX(0)
- Add box-shadow: -4px 0 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.1) on incoming view
- Use will-change: transform for performance
- Add touch gesture support using touchstart/touchmove/touchend for swipe-back
- Use transform3d for GPU acceleration

patterns.name: Navigation Pop
patterns.feelsLike: The current view slides away to the right while the previous view slides back in from the left, restoring context.
useWhen: User taps back button or swipes from left edge
Returning to a previous level in hierarchy

prompts.swiftui:
Create a navigation pop transition in SwiftUI with:
- Spring animation (damping: 0.85, response: 0.35)
- The current view slides out to the right (0% → 100%)
- The previous view slides in from -30% to 0% with opacity 0.8 → 1.0
- Support interactive edge swipe gesture from left
- Use gesture velocity to determine animation completion threshold
- If gesture ends past 40% threshold, complete the pop; otherwise, cancel and spring back
- Match the system NavigationView behavior
prompts.web:
Create a navigation pop transition in HTML/CSS/JS with:
- CSS transition using cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) for spring-like feel
- Duration: 350ms
- Current view: translateX(0) → translateX(100%)
- Previous view: translateX(-30%) opacity 0.8 → translateX(0) opacity 1
- Implement touch gesture on left edge (first 20px)
- Track gesture velocity to determine completion
- Use 40% screen width as threshold for completing vs canceling
- Add box-shadow on departing view for depth

patterns.name: Bottom Sheet Present
patterns.feelsLike: A panel rises from the bottom with a gentle spring, dimming the content behind it.
useWhen: Presenting secondary content that doesn't require full attention
Showing options, filters, or actions related to current context

prompts.swiftui:
Create a bottom sheet presentation in SwiftUI with:
- Use .sheet or custom presentationDetents([.medium, .large])
- Spring animation (damping: 0.8, response: 0.35)
- Sheet slides up from bottom: translateY(100%) → translateY(0)
- Background dims to 30% black with 300ms fade
- Add grab handle (pill indicator) at top of sheet
- Support drag-to-dismiss with velocity-based completion
- Add rubber-banding effect when dragging beyond bounds
- Include presentationDragIndicator(.visible)
prompts.web:
Create a bottom sheet in HTML/CSS/JS with:
- Sheet container: position fixed, bottom 0, left 0, right 0
- Transform: translateY(100%) → translateY(0)
- Transition: transform 350ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)
- Backdrop: position fixed, inset 0, background rgba(0,0,0,0.3)
- Backdrop fade: opacity 0 → 1, 300ms ease-out
- Add 36px wide × 5px tall grab handle with border-radius
- Implement touch drag on handle for dismiss
- Add overscroll rubber-band effect using transform
- Border-radius: 16px 16px 0 0

- Support interactive dismiss with drag gesture
- Use @Namespace for geometry matching
prompts.web:
Create a card-to-fullscreen expand in HTML/CSS/JS with:

- Clone card or use FLIP animation technique
- Animate from original rect to: top 0, left 0, width 100vw, height 100vh
- Transition: all 450ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)
- Border-radius transition: 12px → 0px
- Cross-fade inner content using opacity transitions
- Add backdrop blur on content behind (filter: blur(10px))

- Apply .blur(radius:) or Material for glass effect
- Use linear interpolation for smooth property transitions
- Add .safeAreaInset for proper content layout
- Match iOS 15+ large title navigation bar behavior

patterns.name: Button Press Micro-interaction

- Consider adding subtle shadow reduction on press
prompts.web:
Create a button press micro-interaction in HTML/CSS/JS with:

- Use will-change: transform for smooth animation

patterns.name: Crossfade Between Content States

prompts.swiftui:
Create a crossfade content transition in SwiftUI with:
- Use .transition(.opacity) or custom AnyTransition
- Wrap state change in withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.3))
- Outgoing content: opacity 1 → 0, optional scale 1 → 0.98
- Incoming content: opacity 0 → 1, optional scale 0.98 → 1
- Use .animation(.easeOut, value: contentState) on container
- Consider .contentTransition(.opacity) for Text changes
- For complex views, use .id(stateIdentifier) to force refresh
- Match Android's 'fade through' pattern for cross-platform consistency
prompts.web:
Create a crossfade content transition in HTML/CSS/JS with:

- Outgoing: opacity 1 → 0, transform: scale(1) → scale(0.98)
- Incoming: opacity 0 → 1, transform: scale(0.98) → scale(1)
- Transition: opacity 300ms ease-out, transform 300ms ease-out
- Use 50% overlap (incoming starts fading in at 150ms)
- Alternative: sequential fade-out then fade-in
- Add will-change: opacity for performance

patterns.name: iOS Mail Thread Stack Collapse
patterns.feelsLike: Multiple emails in a thread smoothly stack into a compact preview card with depth layering.
useWhen: Collapsing email thread to show preview of multiple messages
Creating visual hierarchy for grouped content

prompts.swiftui:

- Multiple email cards with decreasing scale and z-offset

- Shadow opacity decreases for cards further back

- Use .matchedGeometryEffect for smooth card transitions
